text: Chronic ankle instability (CAI) is a common sequela of lateral ankle sprain and is associated with recurrent injury, persistent functional limitations, sensorimotor deficits, and impaired postural control. However, how individuals with CAI adapt to graded and combined sensory feedback disruption remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether individuals with CAI exhibit altered postural control during single-leg stance across graded visual, somatosensory, and combined visual-somatosensory disruption compared with healthy controls.
source_label: Postural control responses during single-leg balance in individuals with chronic ankle instability under graded visual and somatosensory disruption
